title: Ex-Broncos quarterback signs with division rival Raiders
text:
NFL news: Raiders sign former Broncos backup quarterback Schedule NFL News Draft Fantasy Odds Betting Newsletter Shop BRONCOS Ex-Broncos quarterback signs with division rival Raiders
 Jon Heath Broncos Wire Nov. 19, 2026, 6:00 a.m. MT After trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings last week, the Las Vegas Raiders added a former Denver Broncos backup quarterback for more depth at the position.
 The Raiders , who turned their offense over to rookie Fernando Mendoza after trading Cousins, signed veteran quarterback Brett Rypien to their practice squad earlier this week. Rypien is set to serve as the third quarterback in Las Vegas behind starter Mendoza and primary backup Aidan O'Connell.
 Rypien, 30, is the nephew of two-time Super Bowl champion Mark Rypien. The younger Rypien entered the league as an undrafted free agent out of Boise State with the Broncos in 2019. He spent the first four years of his NFL career in Denver, going 2-1 as a fill-in starter. Rypien has spent time with 10 other NFL clubs since his stint with the Broncos.
 Elsewhere on the ex-Bronco front, the Cleveland Browns placed fullback Michael Burton on injured reserve; the Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed wide receiver David Sills to their practice squad; wide receiver Samori Toure signed with the Indianapolis Colts' practice squad; defensive back A. J. Woods worked out for the Baltimore Ravens ; kicker Matt Prater had a tryout with the Kansas City Chiefs; tight end Patrick Murtagh worked out for the New Orleans Saints ; running back Blake Watson had a tryout with the Los Angeles Chargers; and defensive lineman Haggai Chisom Ndubuisi signed with the Green Bay Packers' practice squad.
